title.zh: 卷一百八十五 列傳第一百十 鄭二王韋張
title.en: Volume 185 Biographies 110: Zheng, two Wangs, Wei, Zhang
title.raw: 卷一百八十五 列傳第一百十 鄭二王韋張 Volume 185 Biographies 110: Zheng, two Wangs, Wei, Zhang

sentences.zh: 鄭二王韋張

translations.literal: Zheng, the two Wangs, Wei, Zhang
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, the Two Wangs, Wei, and Zhang

sentences.zh: 鄭畋，字臺文，系出滎陽。

translations.literal: Zheng Tian, style name Taiwen, of the Xingyang lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tian, whose courtesy name was Taiwen, came from the Xingyang line of the Zheng clan.

sentences.zh: 父亞，字子佐。

translations.literal: His father was Ya, style name Zizuo.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zheng Ya used the courtesy name Zizuo.

sentences.zh: 爽邁有文，舉進士、賢良方正、書判拔萃，三中其科。

translations.literal: He was bold and free-spirited with literary gifts; he passed the jinshi, xianliang fangzheng, and shupan bacui examinations, achieving distinction in all three categories.
translations.idiomatic: Uninhibited and gifted in letters, he passed the jinshi examination and also excelled in the xianliang fangzheng and shupan bacui competitions, winning distinction in all three.

sentences.zh: 李德裕為翰林學士，高其才，及守浙西，辟署幕府。

translations.literal: When Li Deyu was a Hanlin academician, he esteemed his talent; when he later governed Zhexi, he recruited him to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu, then a Hanlin academician, admired his ability; when Li later held Zhexi, he brought him into his provincial headquarters.

sentences.zh: 擢監察御史，李回任中丞，薦為刑部郎中知雜事，拜給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising censor; when Li Hui became vice censor-in-chief, he recommended him as bureau director of the Ministry of Justice in charge of miscellaneous business, and he was appointed Imperial Attendant-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to supervising censor; when Li Hui served as vice censor-in-chief, Li recommended him as bureau director of the Ministry of Justice with charge of miscellaneous cases, after which he was appointed Imperial Attendant-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 德裕罷宰相，出為桂管觀察使，坐吳湘獄不能直冤，貶循州刺史，死於官。

translations.literal: When Deyu was removed as chief minister and sent out as Guiguan observation commissioner, because in the Wu Xiang case he could not redress the injustice, he was demoted to prefect of Xunzhou and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: After Deyu lost the premiership and was posted to Guiguan as observation commissioner, he was punished in the Wu Xiang affair for failing to secure justice; he was demoted to prefect of Xunzhou and died there in office.

sentences.zh: 畋舉進士，時年甚少，有司上第籍，武宗疑，索所試自省，乃可。

translations.literal: Tian passed the jinshi examination while very young; when the authorities listed him among those who had placed, Wuzong was suspicious and demanded his examination papers from the Ministry of Rites for inspection before approving him.
translations.idiomatic: Tian passed the jinshi while still very young; when the Board listed him among those awarded degrees, Emperor Wuzong was doubtful and had his examination papers brought from the Ministry of Rites for review before confirming the result.

sentences.zh: 奏為宣武推官，以書判拔萃擢渭南尉。

translations.literal: He was memorialized for appointment as legal aide at Xuanwu and, for distinction in shupan, was promoted to assistant magistrate of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: He was nominated as a legal aide at Xuanwu and, on the strength of his shupan bacui standing, was promoted to assistant magistrate of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 父喪免。

translations.literal: He resigned on account of his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 宣宗時，白敏中、令狐繼當國，皆怨德裕，其賓客並廢斥，故畋不調幾十年，外更帥鎮幕府。

translations.literal: In the Xuānzong era, Bai Minzhong and Linghu Tao successively held power; both bore resentment against Deyu, and his clients were alike dismissed and banished, so Tian received no central appointment for several decades and served only in various military commissioners' staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuānzong, Bai Minzhong and Linghu Tao in turn directed the government, each nursing a grudge against Deyu; his associates were all cast out, and for nearly ten years Tian received no capital appointment, serving instead on one frontier commissioner's staff after another.

sentences.zh: 去位，始為虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: Only after they left office did he first become an assistant director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Not until they had left power was he first appointed an assistant director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 右丞鄭薰誣畋罪，不可任郎官，出之。

translations.literal: Vice Director Zheng Xun falsely charged Tian with offenses and declared him unfit to hold a bureau appointment, and he was removed.
translations.idiomatic: The vice director Zheng Xun trumped up charges against Tian, declared him unfit for a bureau post, and had him expelled.

sentences.zh: 久乃入為刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: Only after a long interval was he brought in as assistant director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long interval was he recalled as assistant director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 劉瞻為宰相，薦授戶部郎中，入翰林為學士，俄知制誥。

translations.literal: When Liu Zhan became chief minister, he recommended Tian for appointment as bureau director of the Ministry of Revenue; he entered the Hanlin as academician and soon took charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan, on becoming chief minister, recommended him as bureau director of the Ministry of Revenue; Tian entered the Hanlin Academy as an academician and soon gained charge of drafting imperial pronouncements.

sentences.zh: 會討徐州賊龐勛，書詔紛委，畋思不淹晷，成文粲然，無不切機要，當時推之。

translations.literal: As it happened they were campaigning against Pang Xun, the rebel of Xuzhou; documents and edicts poured in thick and fast; Tian's thoughts never lingered half a day, and his drafts came forth bright and clear, none failing to hit the strategic need—men of the time acclaimed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the court campaigned against Pang Xun of Xuzhou, edicts and orders piled up without respite; Tian never needed more than a day to bring a text to polished completion, and every draft struck exactly what the moment required—contemporaries ranked him first among draftsmen.

sentences.zh: 勛平，以戶部侍郎進學士承旨。

translations.literal: After Xun was pacified, he advanced from vice minister of revenue to Hanlin academician-in-charge.
translations.idiomatic: Once Pang was suppressed, he was promoted from vice minister of revenue to Hanlin academician-in-charge.

sentences.zh: 瞻以諫迕懿宗，賜罷，畋草制書多褒言，韋保衡等怨之，以為附下罔上，貶梧州刺史。

translations.literal: Liu Zhan was impeached and removed for admonishing contrary to Yizong, and the edicts Tian drafted contained much praise; Wei Baoheng and others resented him and charged that he had curried favor below and deceived above, so he was demoted to prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan lost his post after remonstrance angered Emperor Yizong; Tian's draft edicts had spoken highly of him, and Wei Baoheng and others, taking offense, accused Tian of siding with subordinates against superiors and had him demoted to prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 僖宗立，內徙郴、絳二州，以右散騎常侍召還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong ascended, Tian was transferred within the interior to Chen and Jiang prefectures, then summoned back as Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong came to the throne, Tian was moved within the interior to Chen and Jiang, then summoned back as Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 故事，兩省轉對延英，獨常侍不與。

translations.literal: By precedent, when the two departments made successive presentations at the Yanying Hall, the regular attendants alone did not participate.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, when officials of the Secretariat and Chancellery made their rounds of audience at the Yanying Hall, the regular attendants alone were excluded.

sentences.zh: 畋建言宜備顧問，詔可，遂著於令。

translations.literal: Tian submitted that they ought to be available as advisers; the edict approved, and it was written into regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Tian proposed that they too should stand ready as imperial advisers; the throne assented, and the rule was entered in statute.

sentences.zh: 以兵部侍郎進同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: From vice minister of war he advanced to Associate Grand Councilor in the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from vice minister of war to Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 故時，宰相騶哄聯數坊，呵止行人。

translations.literal: In former times, the mounted escorts of chief ministers marched noisily through several wards, shouting to halt passersby.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly a chief minister's outriders would racket through ward after ward, shouting passersby to the curb.

sentences.zh: 畋敕導者止百步，禁百官仆史不得擅至宰相府。

translations.literal: Tian ordered the guides to halt a hundred paces away and forbade officials' servants and clerks from coming uninvited to the chief minister's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Tian directed his ushers to stop a hundred paces short and barred officials' runners and clerks from entering a chief minister's compound without leave.

sentences.zh: 交、廣、邕南兵，舊取嶺北五道米往餉之，船多敗沒。

translations.literal: The armies of Jiao, Guang, and Yongnan had been supplied with grain from the five northern Ling circuits, and many ships were lost in wreck.
translations.idiomatic: Troops in Jiaozhi, Guangzhou, and Yongnan had long been fed with grain shipped from the five northern Ling circuits, and countless transports foundered on the way.

sentences.zh: 畋請以嶺南鹽鐵委廣州節度使韋荷，歲煮海取鹽直四十萬緡，市虔、吉米以贍安南，罷荊、洪等漕役，軍食遂饒。

translations.literal: Tian proposed entrusting Lingnan salt and iron revenues to Wei He, military commissioner at Guangzhou; each year sea salt would yield four hundred thousand strings in cash, which would buy Qian and Ji rice to supply Annan, and transport duties from Jing and Hong would be abolished—thus army provisions grew ample.
translations.idiomatic: Tian urged putting Lingnan salt-and-iron receipts under Guangzhou commissioner Wei He: each year boiling sea salt should raise four hundred thousand strings in cash, with which to purchase Qian and Ji rice for Annan; when the Jing and Hong transport corvées were abolished, the troops at last had food in plenty.

sentences.zh: 後以王師甫為嶺南供軍副使，師甫請兼總兵，而歲加獻錢二十萬緡。

translations.literal: Later Wang Shifu was made deputy supply commissioner for Lingnan; Shifu asked to command troops as well and to present an additional two hundred thousand strings each year.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Shifu was appointed deputy supply commissioner for Lingnan; Shifu asked also to take all military command and to forward an extra two hundred thousand strings annually as tribute.

sentences.zh: 畋曰：「荷且有功，而師甫以利啖朝廷，謀奪其兵，不可。

translations.literal: Tian said: "He has merit already, while Shifu would buy off the court with profit and scheming to seize his forces—that cannot be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Tian said, "Wei He has already done the realm service; Shifu would bribe the court with lucre and scheme to seize his troops—that must not stand."

sentences.zh: 」罷之。

translations.literal: " The proposal was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was struck down.

sentences.zh: 再遷門下侍郎，封滎陽郡侯。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to vice director of the Chancellery and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to vice director of the Chancellery and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 以星變求去位，不許。

translations.literal: On account of portents in the heavens he asked to resign; permission was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Citing prodigies in the sky, he asked to relinquish office; the throne would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 乾符六年，黃巢勢浸盛，據安南，騰書求天平節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qianfu, Huang Chao's strength grew daily; holding Annan, he sent a letter requesting the title of military commissioner of Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Qianfu, Huang Chao's power swelled; he held Annan and sent a memorial demanding the Tianping commission.

sentences.zh: 帝令群臣議，咸請假節以紓難。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the ministers to deliberate; all asked that a provisional commission be granted to ease the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor charged the ministers to debate, and all urged granting him a commission in hope of relief.

sentences.zh: 畋欲因授嶺南節度使，而盧攜方倚高駢，使立功，乃曰：「駢才略無雙，淮南天下勁兵，又諸道之師方至，蕞爾賊，奈何舍之，令四方解體邪？

translations.literal: Tian wished to use the occasion to appoint him military commissioner of Lingnan, but Lu Xie was relying on Gao Pian to win merit, and said: "Pian's talent and stratagem are without equal; Huainan's troops are the strongest in the realm, and armies from every circuit are just arriving—a petty bandit, how can we abandon this and let the four quarters fall apart?"
translations.idiomatic: Tian meant to appoint him commissioner of Lingnan instead, but Lu Xie, counting on Gao Pian to win the day, said, "Pian's genius is unmatched; Huainan commands the realm's finest troops, and columns from every circuit are already marching—why abandon all that over some puny rebels and let the provinces lose heart?"

sentences.zh: 」畋曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Tian said: "That is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Tian replied, "No.

sentences.zh: 巢之亂本於饑，其眾以利合，故能興江、淮，根蔓天下。

translations.literal: Chao's revolt arose from famine; his followers joined for profit, and therefore could flourish in the Yangtze and Huai, with roots and tendrils spreading through the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's uprising began in hunger; his host bands together for gain, which is why they could blaze up along the Jiang-Huai and send roots and runners through the entire empire.

sentences.zh: 國家久平，士忘戰，所在閉壘不敢出。

translations.literal: The state had long been at peace; soldiers forgot warfare; everywhere garrisons shut their ramparts and dared not sally forth.
translations.idiomatic: The empire had known peace so long that fighting men had forgotten war; everywhere outposts shut their walls and would not stir.

sentences.zh: 如以恩釋罪，使及歲豐，其下思歸，眾一離，即巢機上肉耳，法謂不戰而屈人兵也。

translations.literal: If by grace you dismiss their crime and wait until harvest is abundant, his followers will yearn to return home; once the host scatters, Chao will be meat on the chopping block—this is what the Art of War calls subduing the enemy's army without battle.
translations.idiomatic: If you pardon them with grace and wait for a full harvest, his soldiers will long for home; once the masses scatter, Chao will be meat on the chopping block—that is what the Art of War calls defeating the enemy army without fighting.

sentences.zh: 今不伐以謀，而怖以兵，恐天下憂未艾也。

translations.literal: Now, to refrain from strategy that would defeat them and instead frighten them with arms alone— I fear the realm's troubles will not yet end.
translations.idiomatic: If we forgo stratagem and try to scare them with steel alone, I fear the world's worries are nowhere near spent.

sentences.zh: 」僕射於琮言：「南海以寶產富天下，如與賊，國藏竭矣。

translations.literal: " Minister of Works Yu Cong said: "The Southern Sea, rich in treasures, enriches the realm; if it goes to the bandits, the national treasury is drained.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yu Cong said, "The Southern Sea's precious goods enrich the whole realm—hand it to bandits and the national coffers are empty."

sentences.zh: 」天子內亦屬駢，乃然攜議。

translations.literal: " In his heart the Son of Heaven also relied on Pian, and thus Lu Xie's plan was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor too leaned on Pian in private, and Lu Xie's view carried the day.

sentences.zh: 畋曰：「安危屬吾等，而公倚淮南用兵，吾不知所稅駕。

translations.literal: Tian said: "Safety and peril rest with us, yet you rely on troops from Huainan—I do not know where we shall tether our chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Tian said, "The realm's safety rests with us, yet you bank everything on Huainan—I cannot see where this carriage is headed."

sentences.zh: 」會駢奏：「南蠻方強，請如西戎，以公主下嫁。

translations.literal: " Just then Pian memorialized: "The southern barbarians are growing strong; please, as with the western tribes, send a princess down in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Pian memorialized that the southern barbarians were waxing powerful and asked, as with the western tribes, to marry a princess to them.

sentences.zh: 」攜又議從之。

translations.literal: " Xie again urged assent.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xie again urged consent.

sentences.zh: 畋以為損國威靈，不可，即抗論，至相詬嫚。

translations.literal: Tian held that this would injure the state's majesty and could not be done; he disputed heatedly until they exchanged abusive words.
translations.idiomatic: Tian judged it a blow to national majesty and would not hear of it; the dispute grew hot until the two were hurling insults at each other.

sentences.zh: 攜怒，拂衣去，裾蔑於硯，因抵之。

translations.literal: Xie, enraged, swept his robe and left; his hem brushed the inkstone, and he struck it.
translations.idiomatic: Xie stormed out, his sleeve brushing the inkstone, which he struck in passing.

sentences.zh: 帝以大臣爭口語，無以示百官，乃俱罷，以畋為太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: Because great ministers were quarreling in abusive speech with nothing to show the officials, the emperor dismissed them both, appointing Tian Guardian of the Heir Apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed that his chief ministers had come to vulgar shouting before the court, the emperor dismissed them both, naming Tian Guardian of the Heir Apparent with assignment to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 俄召拜吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 明年，為鳳翔隴西節度使，募銳兵五百，號「疾雷將」；

translations.literal: The next year he became military commissioner of Fengxiang Longxi, recruiting five hundred elite troops called the "Swift Thunder Guard";
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became commissioner of Fengxiang and Longxi, recruiting five hundred picked troops dubbed the Swift Thunder Guard;

sentences.zh: 境中盜不敢發，發輒得。

translations.literal: within his circuit bandits did not dare act, and any who did were at once caught.
translations.idiomatic: within his territory no bandit dared strike, and any who did was seized at once.

sentences.zh: 會巢陷東都，遣兵戍京師，以家財勞行，妻自纴戎衣給戰士。

translations.literal: When Chao took the Eastern Capital, he sent troops to garrison the capital; he used family wealth to reward the march, and his wife herself spun military garments for the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao seized the Eastern Capital, Tian dispatched troops to hold the capital; he spent his household fortune on the march and his wife spun military jackets for the men herself.

sentences.zh: 帝出梁、洋，畋上謁斜谷，泣曰：「將相誤國，臣請死以懲無狀。

translations.literal: The emperor fled toward Liang and Yang; Tian met him at Xiegu and wept, saying: "Chief ministers and generals have failed the state; I ask to die to punish my unworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor fled toward Liang and Yang, Tian presented himself at Xiegu in tears: "Ministers and commanders have failed the realm; let me die to answer for our shame."

sentences.zh: 」帝勞遣之，且曰：「公謹扼賊沖，無令得西向。

translations.literal: " The emperor comforted and sent him off, adding: "Sir, diligently block the rebels' thrust—do not let them turn west.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him and sent him off, adding, "Hold the rebels' line with care; do not let them drive west."

sentences.zh: 」畋曰：「方艱虞時，事有機急，不可中覆，請便宜從事，臣當以死報國。

translations.literal: " Tian said: "In time of crisis affairs are urgent; memorials through channels will not do—I ask leave to act on expedient authority; I shall repay the state with my life.
translations.idiomatic: Tian said, "In crisis there is no time for round-trip memorials; grant me discretionary power—my life is pledged to the throne."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「利社稷，無不可。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Whatever profits the altars of soil and grain—there is nothing you may not do.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Whatever serves the altars of state—nothing is forbidden you."

sentences.zh: 」畋還，搜士卒，繕器械，浚城隍，使於梁者道相屬。

translations.literal: " Tian returned, mustered soldiers, repaired weapons, deepened moat and wall, and envoys streaming to Liang stood one upon another on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Tian returned to raise troops, mend arms, deepen moat and wall, and envoys bound for Liang coursed the roads without pause.

sentences.zh: 俄而賊使至，諸將皆欲附賊，畋開諭不可，即悉出金帛，請得脫身去，復不聽。

translations.literal: Before long Chao's emissaries arrived; the generals all wished to join the rebels; Tian reasoned with them that it must not be done; they then offered all their gold and silks and asked leave to depart—they were still not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Huang's envoys arrived; the commanders all thought to go over; Tian argued them back and, when they offered their gold and silks to buy their way out, still refused.

sentences.zh: 而使以偽赦令示軍中乃去。

translations.literal: Only when the emissaries displayed to the army a forged edict of amnesty did they depart.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the envoys showed the troops a forged amnesty edict did they leave.

sentences.zh: 明日，詔使至，畋召監軍袁敬柔以逆順曉諸將，乃聽命，刺血以盟。

translations.literal: The next day an imperial envoy arrived; Tian summoned the army supervisor Yuan Jingrou to teach the generals loyal duty versus rebellion, whereupon they obeyed and pricked blood to seal the covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Next day imperial envoys came; Tian summoned the army supervisor Yuan Jingrou to set loyalty and treason before the commanders; they submitted, and blood sealed the oath.

sentences.zh: 畋遣子凝績從帝，有詔進同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Tian sent his son Ningji to accompany the emperor, and an edict advanced him again to Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Tian sent his son Ningji to attend the emperor; an edict promoted him again to Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 賊將又至，畋斬於軍，餘黨數百人皆捕誅之。

translations.literal: Rebel generals came again; Tian executed them in the army camp and several hundred of their followers were seized and put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel officers came again; Tian beheaded them before the ranks, and several hundred associates were hunted down and killed.

sentences.zh: 遷檢校尚書右僕射、西面行營都統。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and supreme commander of the Western Front camp.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and supreme commander of the Western Front.

sentences.zh: 軍中承制除拜。

translations.literal: Within the army appointments and promotions followed his provisional authority.
translations.idiomatic: In camp he wielded provisional appointment powers.

sentences.zh: 乃以前靈武節度使唐弘夫為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: He then appointed the former commissioner of Lingwu, Tang Hongfu, as camp marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He named the former Lingwu commissioner Tang Hongfu as camp marshal.

sentences.zh: 弘夫取咸陽，以桴濟兵渭水。

translations.literal: Hongfu took Xianyang and ferried his troops across the Wei with rafts.
translations.idiomatic: Hongfu recovered Xianyang and rafted his men across the Wei.

sentences.zh: 賊伏甲偽走，弘夫與宗楚乘勝入都門，為賊所覆。

translations.literal: The rebels hid armor and feigned flight; Hongfu and Zongchu, pressing the advantage, entered the capital gate and were overrun.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels laid an ambush and pretended flight; Hongfu and Zong Chu pressed in through the capital gates and were crushed.

sentences.zh: 畋數敕無輕進，二人不聽，果敗。

translations.literal: Tian had repeatedly ordered them not to advance lightly; the two did not heed him and were indeed defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Tian had warned them repeatedly against rash advance; they ignored him and met defeat.

sentences.zh: 以鄜、夏兵屯東渭橋。

translations.literal: He stationed the Bing and Xia contingents at the Eastern Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: He posted the Bingzhou and Xiazhou forces at the Eastern Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 再進司空、兼門下侍郎、京城四面行營都統，賜禦袍犀帶。

translations.literal: He was advanced again to Grand Preceptor, while retaining the vice directorship of the Chancellery and supreme command of the Four-Side Capital camps, and was given an imperial robe and rhinoceros belt.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Grand Preceptor while retaining the Chancellery vice directorship and supreme command of the capital's four-sided camps, and was granted an imperial robe and rhinoceros-horn belt.

sentences.zh: 拜而不賀。

translations.literal: He accepted the appointment but no congratulations were offered.
translations.idiomatic: He took the seals but received no celebratory visit.

sentences.zh: 行軍司馬李昌言者屯興平，遣麾下求為南面都統，輒引兵趨府。

translations.literal: The camp marshal Li Changyan, encamped at Xingping, sent subordinates to demand appointment as southern front supreme commander and abruptly led troops toward headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Camp marshal Li Changyan, holding Xingping, sent aides demanding the southern supreme command and abruptly marched on headquarters.

sentences.zh: 畋不意見襲，登城好語曰：「吾方入朝，公能戢兵愛人，為國滅賊乎？

translations.literal: Tian, not expecting to be attacked, mounted the wall and spoke in friendly tones: "I am just about to enter court—sir, can you restrain your troops, cherish the people, and destroy the rebels for the state?
translations.idiomatic: Caught by surprise, Tian mounted the wall and said gently, "I am bound for court—can you restrain your men, cherish the people, and destroy the rebels for the realm?"

sentences.zh: 能，則守此矣。

translations.literal: If you can, then keep this post."
translations.idiomatic: If you can, keep this command."

sentences.zh: 」遂委軍去。

translations.literal: " He then entrusted the army and left.
translations.idiomatic: With that he turned the army over and departed.

sentences.zh: 昌言自為留後，衛畋出境。

translations.literal: Changyan declared himself acting commissioner and escorted Tian outside the border.
translations.idiomatic: Changyan made himself acting commissioner and escorted Tian beyond the circuit border.

sentences.zh: 既半道，內慚負，即辭疾。

translations.literal: When halfway along the road inward shame overtook him and he pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: Halfway along the road shame overtook him and he pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 詔授太子少傅，分司東都，便醫於興元。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital, with leave to seek treatment at Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent with assignment to the Eastern Capital and leave to convalesce at Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 明年，召至行在，以王鐸將兵，復拜畋司空、門下侍郎、平章事，軍務一以咨決。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned to the traveling court; as Wang Duo commanded troops, Tian was again appointed Grand Preceptor, vice director of the Chancellery, and Grand Councilor; all military affairs were entrusted to his consultation and decision.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was summoned to the traveling court; with Wang Duo in command of the armies, Tian was again named Grand Preceptor, Chancellery vice director, and Grand Councilor, with every military matter referred to him.

sentences.zh: 興州戍將孫鄴坐贓抵死，畋奏言：「方關輔失守，鄴護褒斜有功，請免死。

translations.literal: Sun Ye, garrison commander of Xingzhou, was sentenced to death for corruption; Tian memorialized: "While the Guanfu region was lost, Ye protected Bao and Xie with merit— I ask that he be spared.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ye, garrison commander of Xingzhou, faced death for graft; Tian wrote, "While the capital approaches were lost, Ye guarded Bao and Xie with merit—spare his life."

sentences.zh: 陳秋兒保嵯峨山拒賊，農不廢耕，請以檢校散騎常侍隸奉天軍。

translations.literal: Chen Qiuer held Mount Cuie to block the rebels; farming was not abandoned— he asked that Qiuer be made Acting Regular Attendant of the Cavalry-in-Waiting and attached to the Fengtian army.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qiuer held Mount Cuie against the rebels without interrupting the fields; Tian asked that he be named Acting Regular Attendant of the Cavalry-in-Waiting and attached to the Fengtian command.

sentences.zh: 」制皆可。

translations.literal: " All edicts were approved.
translations.idiomatic: Both requests were granted.

sentences.zh: 舊制，使府校書郎以上，滿三歲遷；

translations.literal: By old regulation, secretaries and above in commissioners' staffs, after three full years, were transferred;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, staff secretaries and higher ranks in a commissioner's office transferred after three full years;

sentences.zh: 監察御史裏行至大夫、常侍，滿三十月遷。

translations.literal: supervising censors-in-service through administrators and regular attendants, after thirty full months were transferred.
translations.idiomatic: and supervising censors on staff detail through bureau directors and regular attendants transferred after thirty months.

sentences.zh: 雖節度兼宰相，亦不敢越。

translations.literal: Even a commissioner who was also chief minister did not dare overstep this.
translations.idiomatic: Even a commissioner who doubled as chief minister dared not exceed those terms.

sentences.zh: 自軍興，有歲內數遷者，畋以為不可，請：「行營節度，繇裏行至大夫，許滿二十月遷；

translations.literal: Since the armies rose, some were promoted several times within a year; Tian held this unsuitable and requested: "For expedition commissioners, from censor-in-service through administrator, allow transfer after twenty months;
translations.idiomatic: Since war had begun, some men had been promoted several ranks within a year; Tian deemed that wrong and proposed that for expedition commissioners a staff track from censor-in-service through administrator should require twenty months,

sentences.zh: 校書郎以上，滿二歲乃奏。

translations.literal: secretaries and above, after two full years only then might memorial be submitted.
translations.idiomatic: while secretaries and higher should wait two full years before memorial.

sentences.zh: 非軍興者如故事。

translations.literal: Those not under wartime activation follow former precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Peacetime cases should follow the old rules."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 時田令孜恃權有所千請，畋不應。

translations.literal: At the time Tian Lingzi, relying on power, made various private requests; Tian would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi then abused his influence with private asks; Zheng Tian refused them.

sentences.zh: 陳敬瑄欲以官品居宰相上，畋曰：「外宰相安得論品乎？

translations.literal: Chen Jingxuan wished to rank by office grade above the chief ministers; Tian said: "How may an external commissioner argue rank with the chief ministers?
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan wanted to rank his office grade above the chief ministers; Tian said, "How does an outside commissioner argue precedence with the Grand Councilors?"

sentences.zh: 」卒不肯處其下。

translations.literal: " In the end he refused to take a place below him.
translations.idiomatic: To the end he would not stand beneath him.

sentences.zh: 令孜、敬瑄內常銜之。

translations.literal: Lingzi and Jingxuan inwardly often harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi and Jingxuan nursed a steady grudge.

sentences.zh: 賊平，帝將還，而李昌言自以襲畋而奪之鎮，今畋當國，內不喜，故三人相結，而遣客上畋過咎。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified the emperor was about to return; Li Changyan, reflecting that he had seized Tian by surprise and taken his commission while Tian now held power, was inwardly displeased; the three therefore joined forces and sent clients to submit charges of Tian's faults.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed, as the emperor prepared to return, Li Changyan—who had wrested Tian's commission by surprise and now saw Tian back in power—was ill at ease; the three united and sent agents to denounce Tian.

sentences.zh: 帝得其情，不許。

translations.literal: The emperor understood the circumstances and did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw through it and refused.

sentences.zh: 畋乃引疾去位，入見帝曰：「乘輿東還，繇大散關幸鳳翔，供張頓峙，一委昌言，乃可安。

translations.literal: Tian then pleaded illness and resigned, entering audience to say: "When the imperial carriage returns eastward by the route of Great Sanguan Pass to favor Fengxiang, supplies and halts should all be entrusted to Changyan—only then will there be security.
translations.idiomatic: Tian then pleaded illness and resigned, telling the emperor in audience: "When Your Majesty returns east by the Great Sanguan route to Fengxiang, provisions and encampments should rest entirely with Changyan—that is how the journey will be secure."

sentences.zh: 臣若以宰相從，彼且猜阻，非所以靖反側也。

translations.literal: If I follow as chief minister he will be suspicious and obstruct— that is not the way to quiet those who waver in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: If I follow as chief minister he will read it as suspicion—that will not quiet men whose loyalty wavers.

sentences.zh: 請以散官養疾。

translations.literal: I ask to nurse my illness in a nominal office.
translations.idiomatic: Let me keep a nominal title while I convalesce.

sentences.zh: 或群臣有疑，願出臣章示之，使知天子於臣無纖芥者。

translations.literal: If any minister harbors doubt, I wish my memorial be shown them so they know the Son of Heaven bears me not the slightest resentment.
translations.idiomatic: If any minister still doubts, publish my memorial so all know the throne bears me no grudge whatever.

sentences.zh: 」帝以其誠，乃授檢校司徒、太子太保，罷政事。

translations.literal: " The emperor, seeing his sincerity, then appointed him Acting Minister of Works and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and removed him from affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his sincerity, the emperor named him Acting Minister of Works and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and released him from government.

sentences.zh: 以凝績為壁州刺史，留養。

translations.literal: Ningji was appointed prefect of Bi and left to tend him.
translations.idiomatic: Ningji was made prefect of Bi and stayed to care for him.

sentences.zh: 徙龍州，卒，年六十三，贈太尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Longzhou, died, age sixty-three, and was posthumously awarded the title Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to Longzhou, where he died at sixty-three; the court posthumously honored him as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 後帝思畋忠力，又贈太傅。

translations.literal: Later the emperor recalled Tian's loyalty and effort, and additionally posthumously awarded him the title Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Later, remembering Tian's loyal service, the emperor further posthumously ennobled him as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 凝績數歲亦卒。

translations.literal: Ningji also died after several years.
translations.idiomatic: Ningji died as well a few years later.

sentences.zh: 始，李茂貞以博野裨將戍奉天，畋召隸麾下，委以遊邏，厚禮之。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Li Maozhen, as a Boliye deputy general, garrisoned Fengtian; Tian summoned him to serve under his command, entrusted him with mobile patrols, and treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning Li Maozhen was a Boliye subordinate general on garrison duty at Fengtian. Tian brought him into his own command, put him in charge of roaming patrols, and honored him generously.

sentences.zh: 茂貞感其飾擢，及畋還葬鄭，表為請謚曰文昭。

translations.literal: Maozhen was moved by his lavish promotion of him; when Tian returned for burial in Zheng, he submitted a memorial requesting the posthumous title Wenzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen never forgot how Tian had splendidly advanced him; when Tian's body was returned to Zheng for burial, Maozhen memorialized the throne to grant him the posthumous title Wenzhao.

sentences.zh: 天復初，與李思恭配饗僖宗廟廷，又贈宗楚、弘夫官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianfu era, he was paired with Li Sigong in sacrifices at Emperor Xizong's temple hall, and offices were also posthumously awarded to Zongchu and Hongfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the opening years of Tianfu, Tian was paired with Li Sigong in offerings at Emperor Xizong's ancestral temple, and the court also posthumously restored office to Zongchu and Hongfu.

sentences.zh: 畋為人仁恕，姿采如峙玉。

translations.literal: Tian was benevolent and forgiving in person, his bearing like jade standing upright.
translations.idiomatic: Tian was by nature humane and forgiving, with a presence as poised and luminous as polished jade.

sentences.zh: 凡與布衣交，至貴無少易。

translations.literal: Whenever he befriended commoners, even when he reached the highest rank he changed not in the least.
translations.idiomatic: Those he had known as plain commoners found him unchanged in the least even after he rose to the highest honors.

sentences.zh: 鄭縠者，薰子也。

translations.literal: Zheng Gu was Xun's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Gu was the son of Zheng Xun.

sentences.zh: 方畋秉政，擢為給事中，至侍郎。

translations.literal: While Tian held power, he promoted him to Attendant-in-Waiting, up to Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: While Tian directed the government, he raised him from Attendant-in-Waiting all the way to Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 其損怨類如此。

translations.literal: His way of reducing resentment was like this.
translations.idiomatic: This was typical of how he turned old grievances into goodwill.

sentences.zh: 巢之難，先諸軍破賊，雖功不終，而還相天子，坐籌帷幄，終能復國雲。

translations.literal: In Huang Chao's calamity, he was first among the armies to defeat the bandits; though the merit was not brought to completion, he returned to serve the Son of Heaven, sat planning within the tent, and in the end was able to restore the realm.
translations.idiomatic: During Huang Chao's rebellion he was the first of the imperial armies to break the rebels; though victory eluded him in the field, he returned to counsel the emperor from the command tent and in the end helped restore the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 王鐸，字昭範。

translations.literal: Wang Duo, style name Zhaofan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo, whose courtesy name was Zhaofan.

sentences.zh: 宰相播昆弟子也。

translations.literal: He was a nephew of Chancellor Bo's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: He was a nephew on the younger branch of Chancellor Wang Bo's family.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，擢進士第，累遷右補闕、集賢殿直學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Huichang era, he passed the jinshi examination and was successively promoted to Right Remonstrance-censor and Direct Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Huichang period he took the jinshi degree and rose through Right Remonstrance-censor to Direct Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 白敏中辟署西川幕府。

translations.literal: Bai Minzhong recruited him to the Xichuan headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Minzhong brought him onto the staff of the Xichuan headquarters.

sentences.zh: 咸通後，仕浸顯，歷中書舍人、禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: After the Xiantong era, his career gradually became prominent; he served as Secretariat Drafter and Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiantong his career steadily advanced through Secretariat Drafter and Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 所取多才實士，為世稱挹。

translations.literal: Those he selected were mostly men of talent and substance, and were praised and admired by the age.
translations.idiomatic: The men he chose were largely men of real ability, and the world spoke of him with respect.

sentences.zh: 拜御史中丞，以戶部侍郎判度支。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief and served concurrently as Vice Minister of Revenue overseeing the Department of Expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Censor-in-Chief and, as Vice Minister of Revenue, took charge of the Department of Expenditure.

sentences.zh: 十二年，繇禮部尚書進同中書門下平章事，加門下侍郎、尚書左僕射，超拜司徒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, from Minister of Rites he advanced to Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery, was given the additional titles of Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs, and was extraordinarily appointed Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Xiantong he rose from Minister of Rites to Associate Chief Minister, received the additional ranks of Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Left Vice Minister of Works, and was promoted straight to Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 韋保衡緣恩幸輔政，始由鐸得進士，故謹事之。

translations.literal: Wei Baohong entered the government through imperial favor and assisted in affairs of state; he had originally passed the jinshi through Duo's recommendation, so he served him with care.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Baohong had come to power through the emperor's favor; Duo had originally helped him pass the jinshi, and Wei therefore treated him deferentially.

sentences.zh: 雖竊政權，將大斥不附者，病鐸持其事，不得肆，搢紳賴焉。

translations.literal: Although he usurped governmental power and intended to purge greatly those who did not submit, he was hindered by Duo holding matters in check and could not act at will; the gentry relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wei seized real power and meant to drive out all who would not bow to him, Duo checked his hand and kept him from running unchecked, and the court elite took comfort in that.

sentences.zh: 鐸亦上疏祈解，乃以檢校左僕射出為宣武節度使。

translations.literal: Duo also submitted a memorial requesting release from office, and was then made Acting Left Vice Minister of Works and sent out as military commissioner of Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Duo too memorialized asking to be relieved, whereupon he was named Acting Left Vice Minister of Works and posted out as Xuanwu military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 僖宗初，以左僕射召。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xizong's reign, he was recalled as Left Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong first took the throne, Duo was recalled to serve as Left Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 始，鐸當國，練制度，智慮周密，時論推允。

translations.literal: Initially, when Duo directed the state, he was versed in institutions; his plans were thorough and meticulous, and contemporary opinion praised him as fair.
translations.idiomatic: In his first tenure at the helm Duo knew the institutions well, thought with careful precision, and contemporaries judged him sound.

sentences.zh: 會河南盜起，天下跂鐸入輔，又鄭畋數言其賢，復拜門下侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Henan, the whole realm stood on tiptoe hoping Duo would enter to assist; moreover Zheng Tian repeatedly spoke of his talent, and he was again appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion broke out in Henan the empire looked to Duo to return to court, and after Zheng Tian repeatedly praised his ability he was again made Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 乾符六年，賊破江陵，宋威無功，諸將觀望不進，天下大震。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qianfu, the rebels took Jiangling; Song Wei achieved nothing; the generals watched and would not advance; the empire was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Qianfu the rebels overran Jiangling; Song Wei won no success; commanders hung back and refused to move; the realm was convulsed with fear.

sentences.zh: 朝廷議置統帥，鐸因請自率諸將督群盜。

translations.literal: The court debated appointing a supreme commander; Duo thereupon requested to personally lead the generals in suppressing the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated naming a supreme commander, and Duo volunteered to lead the generals himself against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 帝即以鐸為侍中、荊南節度使、諸道行營都統，封晉國公。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately made Duo Palace Attendant, military commissioner of Jingnan, and Supreme Commander of All Circuit Campaign Armies, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once named Duo Palace Attendant and Jingnan military commissioner, made him Supreme Commander of All Circuit Campaign Armies, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Jin.

sentences.zh: 綏納流冗，益募軍，完器鎧，武備張設。

translations.literal: He received and settled displaced refugees, additionally recruited troops, completed armor and weapons, and military preparedness was fully deployed.
translations.idiomatic: He took in displaced people, raised more troops, restored arms and armor, and put the army on a full war footing.

sentences.zh: 李系者，西平王晟諸孫。

translations.literal: Li Xi was a descendant of the Prince of Xiping, Wang Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi was a grandson in the line of Prince Xiping Wang Sheng.

sentences.zh: 敏辯善言兵，然中無有。

translations.literal: He was quick-witted and eloquent and skilled at discussing military matters, yet lacked substance within.
translations.idiomatic: He was sharp-tongued and talked war well, but there was nothing solid behind it.

sentences.zh: 鐸信之，舉為將，分精兵使守湖南。

translations.literal: Duo trusted him, promoted him as a general, and assigned elite troops for him to guard Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Duo believed in him, made him a general, and detached picked troops for him to hold Hunan.

sentences.zh: 俄而賊舍廣州，鼓而北，系望風未戰輒潰，鐸退營襄陽。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels left Guangzhou and marched north with drums beating; Xi fled at the mere sight of them without fighting and collapsed; Duo withdrew his camp to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels quit Guangzhou and marched north to the beat of drums; Xi broke and ran before a blow was struck; Duo pulled back to encamp at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 於是以高駢代之，貶太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gao Pian replaced him; Duo was demoted to Honorary Companion of the Heir Apparent and served at the Eastern Capital in absentia.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian was then put in his place; Duo was demoted to Honorary Companion of the Heir Apparent with nominal duty at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召拜太子少師，從天子入蜀，拜司徒、門下侍郎、平章事，加侍中。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled and appointed Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; he followed the Son of Heaven into Shu, was appointed Minister of Education, Vice Minister of the Chancellery, and Chief Minister, and was given the added title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he was recalled as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and followed the emperor into Shu, where he was made Minister of Education, Vice Minister of the Chancellery, and Chief Minister, with the added rank of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 復以太子太保平章事。

translations.literal: He again served as Chief Minister while holding the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Chief Minister in the capacity of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 是時，誅討大計悉屬駢，駢內幸多難，數偃蹇，而外逗撓。

translations.literal: At that time the grand strategy of extermination devolved entirely on Pian; Pian inwardly had many difficulties with the eunuch favorites, repeatedly being insubordinate, while outwardly he procrastinated and prevaricated.
translations.idiomatic: By then the whole plan to destroy the rebels rested on Gao Pian, who quarreled constantly with the emperor's eunuch favorites and repeatedly dragged his feet while giving every outward sign of delay.

sentences.zh: 鐸感慨王室，每入對，必噫嗚流涕，固請行。

translations.literal: Duo was moved with grief for the imperial house; each time he entered audience he would sigh and weep, and firmly requested to go on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Duo grieved for the throne; at every audience he wept aloud and begged to be sent into the field.

sentences.zh: 時中和二年也。

translations.literal: It was then the second year of Zhonghe.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the second year of Zhonghe.

sentences.zh: 乃以檢校司徒、中書令為義成節度使，諸道行營都統，判延資、戶部、租庸等使。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was made Acting Minister of Education and Grand Preceptor as military commissioner of Yicheng, Supreme Commander of All Circuit Campaign Armies, and concurrently Commissioner of the Yanzi Fund, Revenue, and Corvée-tax.
translations.idiomatic: He was then named Acting Minister of Education and Grand Preceptor, made Yicheng military commissioner and Supreme Commander of All Circuit Campaign Armies, and put in charge of the Yanzi Fund, the Ministry of Revenue, and corvée taxation.

sentences.zh: 於是表崔安潛自副，鄭昌圖、裴贄、裴樞、王摶等在幕府，以周岌、王重榮、諸葛爽、康實、安師儒、時溥六節度為將佐，而中尉西門思恭為監軍，率衛兵洎梁、蜀師三萬壁盩厔，移檄天下。

translations.literal: Thereupon he memorialized Cui Anqian as his deputy; Zheng Changtu, Pei Zuan, Pei Shu, Wang Tuan, and others served in his staff; Zhou Ji, Wang Chongrong, Zhuge Shuang, Kang Shi, An Shiru, and Shi Pu—the six military commissioners—served as his military assistants; Chief Eunuch Ximen Sigong was army supervisor; he led palace guards together with Liang and Shu armies, thirty thousand in all, to encamp at Zhaochi, and issued a proclamation throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He then nominated Cui Anqian as his deputy, gathered Zheng Changtu, Pei Zuan, Pei Shu, Wang Tuan, and others on his staff, and took Zhou Ji, Wang Chongrong, Zhuge Shuang, Kang Shi, An Shiru, and Shi Pu—the six military commissioners—as field lieutenants, with Chief Eunuch Ximen Sigong as army supervisor. With thirty thousand palace guards plus Liang and Shu troops he fortified Zhaochi and sent a call to arms across the empire.

sentences.zh: 先是，諸將雖環賊，莫肯先。

translations.literal: Previously, although the generals had surrounded the rebels, none would take the lead.
translations.idiomatic: Before this the generals had hemmed in the rebels but none would strike first.

sentences.zh: 及鐸檄至，號令殷然，士氣皆起，急欲破賊，故巢戰數蹙。

translations.literal: When Duo's proclamation arrived, orders resounded impressively; morale rose everywhere; all urgently wished to break the rebels; therefore Huang Chao's forces were repeatedly pressed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Duo's proclamation went out, commands rang with authority, spirits lifted, and every man burned to smash the rebels, so Huang Chao's army was driven back again and again.

sentences.zh: 宦人田令孜策賊必破，欲使功出於己，乃構鐸於帝，罷為檢校司徒，以義成節度還屯。

translations.literal: The eunuch Tian Lingzi calculated that the rebels would certainly be broken and wished the merit to issue from himself; he therefore slandered Duo to the emperor; Duo was removed as Acting Minister of Education, retained his Yicheng commission, and returned to garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Tian Lingzi, sure the rebels would fall, wanted the credit for himself; he poisoned the emperor's mind against Duo, stripped him of the Acting Minister of Education title, and left him only as Yicheng commissioner in camp.

sentences.zh: 鐸功危就，而讒見奪，然卒因其勢困賊。

translations.literal: Duo's merit was near completion, yet he was removed on slander; still, in the end they took advantage of the momentum he had created to distress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Duo was on the verge of success when slander cost him command, yet in the end others used the momentum he had built to corner the rebels.

sentences.zh: 後數月，復京師，策勛居關東諸鎮第一。

translations.literal: Several months later the capital was recovered; in reckoning merit he ranked first among the eastern circuits.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later the capital was retaken, and when honors were apportioned Duo stood first among the eastern commands.

sentences.zh: 四年，徙義昌節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred as military commissioner of Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to serve as Yichang military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鐸世貴，出入裘馬鮮明，妾侍且眾。

translations.literal: Duo came from an aristocratic family; going out and in he was splendid in fur coats and horses, and his concubine attendants were many.
translations.idiomatic: Duo was born to great wealth; he traveled in bright furs and fine horses and kept a large household of concubines.

sentences.zh: 過魏，樂彥禎子從訓心利之。

translations.literal: Passing through Wei, Le Yanzhen's son Congxun coveted his wealth in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: When he passed through Wei, Le Yanzhen's son Congxun set his heart on Duo's riches.

sentences.zh: 李山甫者，數舉進士被黜，依魏幕府，內樂禍，且怨中朝大臣，導從訓以詭謀，使伏兵高雞泊劫之，鐸及家屬吏佐三百餘人皆遇害。

translations.literal: Li Shanfu had repeatedly taken the jinshi examination and been failed; he relied on Wei's headquarters; inwardly he delighted in calamity and also resented the court's grand ministers; he guided Congxun with cunning plots, had hidden troops ambush at Gaojipo and rob them; Duo and more than three hundred family members, clerks, and aides were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shanfu had failed the jinshi again and again and lived on Wei's staff; he welcomed disaster and hated the great ministers at court. He fed Congxun a treacherous plan, set an ambush at Gaojipo, and waylaid the party. Duo and more than three hundred kin, clerks, and attendants were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 朝廷微弱，不能治其冤，天下痛之。

translations.literal: The court was weak and could not redress the injustice; the whole realm grieved for it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne was too feeble to avenge the crime, and the empire mourned.

sentences.zh: 弟鐐，累官汝州刺史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Liao cumulatively served as prefect of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wang Liao rose to become prefect of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，王仙芝來攻，鐐拒之，自督勇士與別將董漢勛守南、北門。

translations.literal: In the Qianfu era, Wang Xianzhi came to attack; Liao resisted him, personally directing brave soldiers together with deputy general Dong Hanxun in guarding the south and north gates.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianfu, when Wang Xianzhi besieged the city, Liao held him off, personally leading picked men with deputy commander Dong Hanxun at the south and north gates.

sentences.zh: 城陷，漢勛力戰死，鐐貶韶州司馬。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Hanxun fought fiercely and died; Liao was demoted to secretary of Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the walls gave way Hanxun fought to the death; Liao was demoted to secretary of Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 終太子賓客。

translations.literal: He eventually served as Honorary Companion of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Honorary Companion of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 王徽，字昭文，京兆人。

translations.literal: Wang Hui, style name Zhaowen, a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui, courtesy name Zhaowen, was a native of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 第進士，授校書郎。

translations.literal: He placed in the jinshi examination and was appointed collator.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a collator.

sentences.zh: 沈詢判度支，徐商領鹽鐵，皆辟署使府。

translations.literal: Shen Xun oversaw the Department of Expenditure and Xu Shang headed Salt and Iron; both recruited him to their commissioner staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Xun, who ran the Department of Expenditure, and Xu Shang, who headed Salt and Iron, both brought him onto their commissioner staffs.

sentences.zh: 始，宣宗詔宰相選可尚主者，或以徽聞。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Emperor Xuanzong ordered the chancellors to select those suitable to marry a princess; someone mentioned Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Emperor Xuanzong told his chancellors to choose men fit to marry a princess, and Hui's name was put forward.

sentences.zh: 徽本淡聲利，聞不喜，往見宰相劉彖曰：「徽年過四十，又多病，不應在選。

translations.literal: Hui was originally indifferent to fame and profit; on hearing this he was not pleased; he went to see Chancellor Liu Yan and said, "Hui is past forty and has many illnesses; he should not be among those selected.
translations.idiomatic: Hui cared little for rank or gain and took no pleasure in the news; he went to Chancellor Liu Yan and said, "I am past forty and often ill—I am no fit candidate.

sentences.zh: 」彖為言，乃罷。

translations.literal: " Yan spoke on his behalf, and the matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu pleaded his case, and the selection was dropped.

sentences.zh: 從令狐署宣武、淮南掌書記，召授右拾遺。

translations.literal: He followed Linghu Tao as secretarial aide at Xuanwu and Huainan; he was summoned and appointed Right Collector of Remonstrances.
translations.idiomatic: He served Linghu Tao as secretarial aide at Xuanwu and Huainan, then was recalled and made Right Collector of Remonstrances.

sentences.zh: 書二十餘上，言無回忌，公議浩然歸重。

translations.literal: He submitted more than twenty memorials, speaking without reserve or fear; public opinion resoundingly turned respect to him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent up more than twenty memorials, speaking bluntly and without fear, and public esteem for him grew strong.

sentences.zh: 徐商罷政事，守江陵，心欲表徽在幕府，恐其不樂外，忍不言。

translations.literal: Xu Shang left the government and guarded Jiangling; in his heart he wished to memorialize Hui to remain on his staff, but feared Hui would not enjoy being outside the capital and endured without speaking.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Shang left court to guard Jiangling he wanted to keep Hui on his staff but feared Hui would dislike provincial service, and so he held his tongue.

sentences.zh: 徽自往曰：「公知徽，安得不從？

translations.literal: Hui went to him himself and said, "You know Hui—how could I not follow?
translations.idiomatic: Hui came to him and said, "You know me—how could I refuse?

sentences.zh: 」商大喜，表為殿中侍御史，署節度府判官。

translations.literal: " Shang was greatly pleased; he memorialized him as Palace Censor and appointed him legal officer of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu was delighted, recommended him as Palace Censor, and made him legal officer of the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞高湜薦知雜事，進考功員外郎。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Gao Yan recommended him to handle miscellaneous business, and he was promoted to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Gao Yan put him in charge of miscellaneous cases, and he rose to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 故事，考簿以朱註上下為殿最，歲久易漫，吏輒竄易為奸。

translations.literal: By precedent, evaluation records used cinnabar to note superior and inferior for first and last rankings; over the years they easily faded, and clerks would fraudulently alter them for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, personnel files marked top and bottom ranks in cinnabar ink; over time the marks faded and clerks tampered with them for profit.

sentences.zh: 徽始用墨，遂絕妄欺。

translations.literal: When Hui first used ink, false alterations were then ended.
translations.idiomatic: Hui switched to black ink, and the fraud stopped.

sentences.zh: 擢翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 廣明元年，盧攜罷宰相，以徽為戶部侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangming, Lu Xie was dismissed as chancellor; Hui was made Vice Minister of Revenue and Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangming, when Lu Xie was removed as chancellor, Hui was made Vice Minister of Revenue and Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 是日，黃巢入關，僖宗西狩，冒夜出。

translations.literal: That day, Huang Chao entered the pass; Emperor Xizong hunted westward and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Huang Chao broke through the pass; Emperor Xizong fled west and stole away in the night.

sentences.zh: 徽與崔沆、豆盧彖、僕射於琮詰朝乃知，追帝不及，墮崖樾間，為賊所執，迫還，將汙以官。

translations.literal: Hui together with Cui Hang, Doulu Yan, and Vice Director Yu Cong only learned at the morning audience; pursuing the emperor they could not catch up; he fell among cliff trees, was captured by rebels, was forced to return, and was about to be defiled with office.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, Cui Hang, Doulu Yan, and Vice Director Yu Cong learned of the flight only at the morning audience; they raced after the emperor but could not overtake him. Hui fell among cliffs and trees, was seized by rebels, dragged back, and was to be forced into office under them.

sentences.zh: 徽陽喑不答，以刃環脅，卒不動。

translations.literal: Hui pretended to be mute and answered not; they used ringed blades to threaten him, yet in the end he did not move.
translations.idiomatic: Hui feigned muteness and would not reply; they threatened him with ringed blades, but he never yielded.

sentences.zh: 賊令歸第，使醫護視。

translations.literal: The rebels ordered him to return home and sent a physician to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent him home and posted a doctor to watch over him.

sentences.zh: 久之，守者懈，乃奔河中，裂縑書章，遣人間走蜀。

translations.literal: After a long while the guards relaxed; then he fled to Hezhong, tore silk to write a memorial seal, and sent a man by secret routes to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When the guards slackened he fled to Hezhong, tore silk into strips to compose a sealed memorial, and sent a messenger by hidden paths into Shu.

sentences.zh: 詔拜兵部尚書、京城四面宣慰催陣使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Minister of War, Pacification and Rally Commissioner on Four Sides of the Capital City, and Urgent-Battle Formation Officer.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him Minister of War and Commissioner for Pacifying and Rallying the Four Quarters of the Capital, charged with pressing the battle lines.

sentences.zh: 昭義高潯與賊戰石橋，敗績。

translations.literal: Gao Xun of Zhaoyi fought the rebels at Shiqiao and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xun of Zhaoyi fought the rebels at Shiqiao and suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 其將劉廣擅還，據潞州。

translations.literal: His general Liu Guang returned on his own authority and seized Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His general Liu Guang withdrew on his own and seized Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 別將孟方立殺廣，因取邢、洺、磁三州貳於己。

translations.literal: Deputy general Meng Fangli killed Guang and then took the three prefectures Xing, Ming, and Ci as his own separate domain.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Meng Fangli killed Liu Guang and then kept Xing, Ming, and Ci for himself in defiance of the court.

sentences.zh: 昭義所隸，唯澤一州。

translations.literal: Of Zhaoyi's subordinate prefectures, only Ze remained.
translations.idiomatic: Of all Zhaoyi's territory, only Ze Prefecture still obeyed the court.

sentences.zh: 帝以兵部侍郎鄭昌圖權守潞，士心多附方立，昌圖不能制。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Vice Minister of War Zheng Changtu to hold Luzhou temporarily; popular sentiment largely attached to Fangli, and Changtu could not control it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put Vice Minister of War Zheng Changtu in temporary charge of Luzhou, but the soldiers' loyalty leaned to Fangli and Changtu could not master the situation.

sentences.zh: 朝議以大臣鎮撫，即授徽檢校尚書左僕射、同中書門下平章事，領昭義節度使。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that a grand minister should pacify the region; Hui was immediately appointed Acting Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs, Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and head of Zhaoyi as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court decided a senior minister should restore order, and Hui was at once named Acting Left Vice Minister of Works, Associate Chief Minister, and Zhaoyi military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是時，李克用亦爭澤、潞，徽商朝廷力未能以兵抗之，奉表固辭，詔可。

translations.literal: At that time Li Keyong also contended for Ze and Lu; Hui discussed with the court that its strength was insufficient to resist with troops; he submitted a memorial firmly declining, and the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong was also fighting for Ze and Lu; Hui told the court it lacked the force to resist and firmly declined the post by memorial; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 更為諸道租庸供軍使。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Commissioner for Corvée-tax Supply to the Armies of All Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Commissioner for supplying corvée tax to the armies of all circuits.

sentences.zh: 因說行營都監楊復光，請赦沙陀罪，令赴難。

translations.literal: He then persuaded the Supreme Army Supervisor Yang Fuguang to request amnesty for the Shatuo's crime and summon them to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: He then urged Supreme Army Supervisor Yang Fuguang to ask pardon for the Shatuo and call them to the empire's aid.

sentences.zh: 其夏，沙陀會諸軍，遂平京師，徽助為多，遷右僕射。

translations.literal: That summer the Shatuo joined the armies and then pacified the capital; Hui contributed greatly, and he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the Shatuo joined the allied armies and retook the capital; Hui's help was great, and he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 大亂之後，宮觀焚殘，園陵皆發掘，鞠為丘莽，乘輿未有東意，詔徽充大明宮留守、京畿安撫制置脩奉使。

translations.literal: After the great chaos, palaces and temples were burned and ruined, imperial tombs were all excavated, and the ground was turned to mounds and wastes; the imperial carriage had not yet the intention of returning east; an edict appointed Hui as Guardian of Daming Palace, Commissioner for Pacifying and Managing Restoration and Repair of the Capital Region.
translations.idiomatic: After the great upheaval palaces and temples lay in ashes, imperial tombs had been opened and looted, and the land was heaped rubble; the emperor still showed no wish to return east. Hui was ordered to serve as Guardian of Daming Palace and Commissioner for Pacifying, Organizing, and Restoring the Capital Region.

sentences.zh: 徽外調兵食，內撫綏流亡，逾年，稍稍完聚，興復殿寢，裁制有宜，即奉表請帝東還。

translations.literal: Externally he requisitioned troops and provisions; internally he soothed and settled refugees; after more than a year, things were gradually restored and gathered; he rebuilt palace halls and sleeping quarters with appropriate measures, and then submitted a memorial requesting the emperor return east.
translations.idiomatic: He raised troops and grain from outside while comforting refugees within; after more than a year the city slowly came back to life, palace halls were rebuilt with sound judgment, and he memorialized asking the emperor to return east.

sentences.zh: 又進檢校司空、御史大夫，仍權京兆尹。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to Acting Minister of Works and Censor-in-Chief, and still served concurrently as acting governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Acting Minister of Works and Censor-in-Chief and continued as acting Jingzhao governor.

sentences.zh: 宦要家爭遣人治第，侵冒齊民，訟訴滿前，徽不屈勢幸，一平以法，繇是為帝左右所憎，以其黨薛杞為少尹，輕其權。

translations.literal: Powerful eunuch families competed to send people to build mansions, encroaching on common people; lawsuits filled his desk; Hui did not yield to powerful favorites and leveled all according to law; thereby he was hated by those around the emperor; his faction had Xue Qi made Junior Governor to lighten his authority.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch grandees vied to build mansions that encroached on commoners' land, and Hui's docket overflowed with suits; he would not bend to the powerful and applied the law evenly. For this the emperor's intimates turned against him; they installed his rival Xue Qi as Junior Governor to cut his power.

sentences.zh: 杞方居喪，徽奏止不使到府。

translations.literal: Qi was in mourning; Hui memorialized to stop him from coming to the office.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was in mourning, and Hui memorialized to bar him from taking up office.

sentences.zh: 眾忿，共譖罷徽，令赴行在。

translations.literal: The masses were enraged; jointly they slandered to remove Hui and ordered him to proceed to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: His enemies were furious; they joined in slander to remove him and ordered him to the emperor's traveling court.

sentences.zh: 俄授太子少師。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 徽遂移疾河中，滿百日免。

translations.literal: Hui then submitted illness at Hezhong; after a hundred days he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then pleaded illness at Hezhong and, after the hundred-day term, was released from office.

sentences.zh: 帝還京師，復申前授，稱疾不任奉謁。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital, he re-offered the previous appointment; Hui claimed illness and could not undertake court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor came back to the capital he renewed the old appointment, but Hui pleaded illness and declined to attend court.

sentences.zh: 宰相疾其怨望，貶集州刺史。

translations.literal: The chancellor resented his resentment and demoted him to prefect of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister, angered by what he took for sullen discontent, demoted Hui to prefect of Ji.

sentences.zh: 會帝避沙陀，出次寶雞。

translations.literal: When the emperor avoided the Shatuo, he went out and encamped at Baoji.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fled the Shatuo threat he withdrew and halted at Baoji.

sentences.zh: 帝念徽無罪，拜吏部尚書，封瑯邪郡侯。

translations.literal: The emperor remembered that Hui was innocent; he appointed him Minister of Personnel and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Langye Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering that Hui had done no wrong, the emperor named him Minister of Personnel and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Langye.

sentences.zh: 未行而嗣襄王煴作亂，帝進次漢中。

translations.literal: Before he had set out, the heir Xiang Wang Yun raised rebellion, and the emperor advanced and halted at Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Before Hui could take up the post, Li Yun, claimant to the title of Xiang Wang, rebelled, and the emperor withdrew to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 煴逼召徽，以尫廢自言。

translations.literal: Yun forced and summoned Hui; he declared himself weak and disabled.
translations.idiomatic: Yun urgently summoned Hui, who pleaded that he was feeble and crippled.

sentences.zh: 及煴僭號，迫群臣作誓牒，徽托手弱，卒不肯署。

translations.literal: When Yun usurped the title, he forced the ministers to draw up pledge documents; Hui pleaded weak hands, and in the end refused to sign.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun declared himself emperor, he forced the officials to sign pledge documents; Hui claimed his hands were too weak to write and ultimately refused to sign.

sentences.zh: 煴平，帝至鳳翔，召徽為御史大夫，固辭足痺，復拜太子少師。

translations.literal: When Yun was suppressed, the emperor reached Fengxiang, summoned Hui as Censor-in-Chief; he firmly declined citing foot paralysis, and was again appointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After Yun's rebellion was crushed, the emperor reached Fengxiang and summoned Hui to serve as Censor-in-Chief; Hui firmly declined, citing paralysis in his legs, and was instead reappointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 昭宗立，見便殿，進對詳洽，帝顧宰相曰：「徽神氣尚強，可用。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong ascended, Hui was received in the informal hall; his responses were thorough and apt; the emperor turned to the chancellor and said: "Hui's spirit is still strong — he can be used.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong took the throne, Hui was received in the informal hall; his answers were thorough and fluent. The emperor turned to the chancellor and said, "Hui's vigor is still strong — he can be put to use.

sentences.zh: 」乃復授吏部尚書。

translations.literal: " And so he was again appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: " He was accordingly reappointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 是時，銓選失序，吏肆為奸，補調重復不可檢。

translations.literal: At that time selection and appointment were in disorder; clerks indulged in fraud; duplicate appointments and transfers could not be checked.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the appointment rolls were in chaos: clerks ran wild with fraud, and duplicate postings and transfers could no longer be audited.

sentences.zh: 徽為手藉，一驗實之，遂無奸滯。

translations.literal: Hui made a handwritten register, verified each entry one by one, and thereby eliminated fraud and backlog.
translations.idiomatic: Hui compiled a handwritten register and checked every entry against the facts, clearing away fraud and backlog alike.

sentences.zh: 進右僕射。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 大順元年卒，贈司空，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dashun he died; posthumously awarded Minister of Works; posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Dashun and was posthumously awarded Minister of Works with the posthumous title Zhen.

sentences.zh: 譜言其先本魏諸公子，秦滅魏，至漢徙關中霸陵，以其故王家，為王氏。

translations.literal: The genealogy says his forebears were originally sons of a prince of Wei; when Qin destroyed Wei, by Han times they moved to Balin in Guanzhong; because they were formerly a royal house, they took the surname Wang.
translations.idiomatic: The family genealogy records that his ancestors were originally sons of a Wei prince; after Qin destroyed Wei, they moved by Han times to Balin in Guanzhong, and because they had once been a royal house they took the surname Wang.

sentences.zh: 十世祖羆，仕周為同州刺史，死葬咸陽鳳政原，子孫因家杜陵。

translations.literal: His tenth-generation ancestor Pi served Zhou as prefect of Tongzhou; he died and was buried at Fengzheng Plain in Xianyang; descendants then made their home at Dulung.
translations.idiomatic: His tenth-generation ancestor Pi served the Zhou dynasty as prefect of Tongzhou; after he died and was buried on Fengzheng Plain in Xianyang, his descendants settled at Dulung.

sentences.zh: 曾祖擇從，昆弟四人，曰易從、朋從、言從，皆擢進士第。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zecong had four brothers named Yicong, Pengcong, and Yancong; all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zecong was one of four brothers — Yicong, Pengcong, and Yancong being the others — and all four passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 至鳳閣舍人者三人，故號「鳳閣王氏」。

translations.literal: Three reached the post of Fengge Attendant; hence the name "Wang of Fengge."
translations.idiomatic: Three of them rose to the post of Fengge Attendant, and for this reason the clan was known as "the Wang of Fengge."

sentences.zh: 自是訖大中時，登進士者十八人，位臺省牧守者三十餘人。

translations.literal: From then until the Dazhong era, eighteen passed the jinshi examination and more than thirty held posts in the central administration or as regional governors.
translations.idiomatic: From that time down to the Dazhong era, eighteen clan members passed the jinshi examination and more than thirty held posts in the central administration or as regional governors.

sentences.zh: 徽有雅望，拜宰相一日而京師亂，故其設施無可道者。

translations.literal: Hui enjoyed refined reputation; he served as chancellor one day and then the capital fell into chaos, so there was nothing noteworthy in his measures.
translations.idiomatic: Hui enjoyed a fine reputation, but he served as chancellor for only a day before the capital fell into chaos, so there was little worth recording in his official career.

sentences.zh: 韋昭度，字正紀，京兆人。

translations.literal: Wei Zhaodu, courtesy name Zhengji, was a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhaodu, courtesy name Zhengji, was a native of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，踐歷華近，累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, served in prized posts near the throne, and was promoted repeatedly to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, served in prestigious posts close to the throne, and was promoted step by step to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 僖宗西狩，以兵部侍郎、翰林學士承旨從。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong fled west, he followed as Vice Minister of War and Hanlin Academician in Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong fled west, Zhaodu accompanied him as Vice Minister of War and Chief Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 未幾，同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he became co-chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed co-chancellor.

sentences.zh: 還京，授司空。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital he was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the capital he was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 再狩山南，還次鳳翔。

translations.literal: When the emperor again fled to the mountains south, they returned and halted at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor again fled south of the mountains, the court withdrew and halted at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 李昌符亂興倉卒，昭度質家族於禁軍，誓共討賊，士感動，乃平昌符。

translations.literal: When Li Changfu's rebellion erupted suddenly, Zhaodu pledged his family as hostages to the imperial guard, swore to join in suppressing the rebel, the troops were moved, and thus Changfu was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Changfu's rebellion broke out in haste, Zhaodu left his family as hostages with the imperial guard and swore to join in suppressing the rebel; the troops were deeply moved, and Changfu was duly pacified.

sentences.zh: 遷太保，兼侍中。

translations.literal: He was moved to Grand Mentor and concurrently Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Mentor and concurrently appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 昭宗即位，守中書令，封岐國公。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong took the throne, he held the post of Grand Councilor and was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong took the throne, Zhaodu served as Grand Councilor and was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 閬州刺史王建攻陳敬瑄於成都，以昭度為西川節度使。

translations.literal: Wang Jian, prefect of Langzhou, besieged Chen Jingxuan at Chengdu; Zhaodu was made military governor of Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, prefect of Langzhou, besieged Chen Jingxuan at Chengdu, and Zhaodu was appointed military governor of Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄不內，詔東川顧彥朗與建合兵以討，拜昭度兼行營招撫使。

translations.literal: Jingxuan would not admit him; an edict ordered Gu Yanlang of Dongchuan to join Wang Jian's forces to suppress him; Zhaodu was additionally appointed Pacification Commissioner of the mobile camp.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan refused to admit him; the court ordered Gu Yanlang of Dongchuan to join Wang Jian's forces in the campaign and additionally appointed Zhaodu Pacification Commissioner of the mobile camp.

sentences.zh: 乃建幢節行城下，諭其眾曰：「毋久閉壘。

translations.literal: Then he raised banners and insignia beneath the walls and addressed the garrison: "Do not long keep the fortresses closed.
translations.idiomatic: He then raised banners and insignia beneath the city walls and addressed the garrison: "Do not keep your defenses shut for long.

sentences.zh: 」敬瑄遣人詈曰：「鐵券，先帝所命，若何違之？

translations.literal: " Jingxuan sent someone to curse back: "The iron certificate was conferred by the late emperor — how dare you violate it?
translations.idiomatic: " Jingxuan sent a messenger to revile him in reply: "The iron certificate was granted by the late emperor — how dare you defy it?

sentences.zh: 」淹半歲，始拔漢州。

translations.literal: " After half a year they finally captured Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " After half a year they finally took Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 建紿昭度曰：「公暴師遠出，事蠻夷地，方山東兵連禍結，朝廷不能治，腹心疾也，宜亟還定之。

translations.literal: Wang Jian deceived Zhaodu, saying: "You have exposed your armies on a distant campaign in barbarian territory; meanwhile calamities multiply in the east and the court cannot govern — this is a disease of the heartland; you should hurry back to stabilize it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian deceived Zhaodu, saying, "You have marched your army far abroad into barbarian country, while disasters multiply in the east and the court cannot govern — this is a sickness at the empire's heart; you should hurry back to restore order there.
