sentences.zh: 敬瑄小鬼，當責建等可辨。

translations.literal: Jingxuan is a petty ghost; charge me and my men and we shall deal with him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan is a petty foe — leave him to me and my men and we shall settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 」昭度信之，請還。

translations.literal: " Zhaodu believed him and requested to return.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhaodu believed him and asked to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 未半道，建以重兵守劍門，急攻成都。

translations.literal: Before he was halfway back, Wang Jian held Jianmen Pass with heavy troops and pressed the attack on Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhaodu was halfway home, Wang Jian sealed Jianmen Pass with a heavy force and pressed the attack on Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 囚敬瑄，自稱留後。

translations.literal: He imprisoned Jingxuan and declared himself acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: He imprisoned Jingxuan and declared himself acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 罷昭度為東都留守。

translations.literal: Zhaodu was removed and made Guardian of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaodu was removed from office and appointed Guardian of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 杜讓能既被害，以司徒、門下侍郎復為平章事，進太傅。

translations.literal: After Du Rangneng had been killed, Zhaodu was restored as chancellor as Secretary of State and Vice Director of the Chancellery, and advanced to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: After Du Rangneng had been killed, Zhaodu was restored to the chancellorship as Secretary of State and Vice Director of the Chancellery and was promoted to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 王行瑜求為尚書令，昭度建言：「太宗由是即位，後人臣無復拜者。

translations.literal: Wang Xingyu sought the post of Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Zhaodu advised: "Taizong came to the throne through that office; afterward no subject was ever again appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingyu sought appointment as Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Zhaodu advised, "Taizong came to the throne through that office, and afterward no subject was ever again given it.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀有大功，嘗授之，固辭免，況行瑜乎？

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi, though he had great merit, was once offered it and firmly declined; how much more so for Xingyu?
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi, for all his great merit, was once offered the post and firmly declined — how much less should Xingyu receive it?

sentences.zh: 」乃更號尚父。

translations.literal: " So another title, Revered Father, was granted instead.
translations.idiomatic: " He was given the alternate title of Revered Father instead.

sentences.zh: 行瑜怨。

translations.literal: Xingyu resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu resented the refusal.

sentences.zh: 會用李磎輔政，而崔昭緯密語行瑜曰：「前公已為尚書令，昭度持不可。

translations.literal: When Li Xi was used to assist in government, Cui Zhaowei secretly told Xingyu: "You had already been made Director of the Imperial Secretariat, but Zhaodu insisted it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xi was brought in to assist in government, Cui Zhaowei secretly told Xingyu, "You had already been made Director of the Imperial Secretariat, but Zhaodu blocked it.

sentences.zh: 今又引磎葉力，此奸人務立黨與，惑上聽，恐事復有如杜太尉時。

translations.literal: Now he brings in Li Xi and Ye Li; these schemers are bent on building factions and misleading the emperor — I fear events will repeat those at the time of Grand Marshal Du.
translations.idiomatic: Now he is bringing in Li Xi and Ye Li — schemers bent on building factions and misleading the throne. I fear we shall see a repeat of what happened to Grand Marshal Du.

sentences.zh: 」行瑜乃與李茂貞數上書譏詆朝政。

translations.literal: " Xingyu then joined Li Maozhen in repeatedly submitting memorials ridiculing and denouncing court governance.
translations.idiomatic: " Xingyu then joined Li Maozhen in repeatedly submitting memorials ridiculing and denouncing the court.

sentences.zh: 昭度懼，稱疾，罷為太傅，致仕。

translations.literal: Zhaodu grew afraid, pleaded illness, was removed to Grand Preceptor, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaodu grew afraid, pleaded illness, was removed to Grand Preceptor, and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 行瑜、茂貞、韓建聯兵至闕下，言昭度伐蜀失謀，請貶之。

translations.literal: Xingyu, Maozhen, and Han Jian joined forces to the palace gates, saying Zhaodu's Sichuan campaign had failed through bad planning and requesting his demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu, Maozhen, and Han Jian joined forces and marched to the palace gates, charging that Zhaodu's Sichuan campaign had failed through bad planning and demanding his demotion.

sentences.zh: 未及報，而行瑜收昭度於都亭驛殺之。

translations.literal: Before a reply could be sent, Xingyu seized Zhaodu at the Capital Pavilion Station and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Before the court could respond, Xingyu seized Zhaodu at the Capital Pavilion Station and killed him.

sentences.zh: 天子不得已，下詔暴其罪。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, with no choice, issued an edict publicly listing his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, left with no choice, issued an edict publicly listing Zhaodu's crimes.

sentences.zh: 行瑜誅，乃追復官爵，許其家收葬，贈太尉。

translations.literal: When Xingyu was executed, Zhaodu's offices and titles were posthumously restored, his family was allowed to retrieve his body for burial, and he was posthumously awarded Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingyu was executed, Zhaodu's offices and titles were posthumously restored, his family was permitted to recover his body for burial, and he was posthumously awarded the title of Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 張濬，字禹川，本河間人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun, courtesy name Yuchuan, was originally from Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, courtesy name Yuchuan, was originally from Hejian.

sentences.zh: 性通脫無檢，泛知書史，喜高論，士友擯薄之。

translations.literal: His nature was unrestrained and undisciplined; he had broad but superficial knowledge of books and history and loved lofty talk; scholar-friends shunned and looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Unrestrained and undisciplined by nature, he had a broad but shallow knowledge of books and history and loved grand talk; men of learning shunned and looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 不得志，乃羸服屏居金鳳山，學從橫術，以捭闔幹時。

translations.literal: Frustrated, he wore humble clothes and withdrew to Mount Jinfeng, studied coalition diplomacy, and sought to sway the age by intrigue.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated in his ambitions, he put on humble dress and withdrew to Mount Jinfeng, where he studied coalition diplomacy and sought to win his way in the world through intrigue.

sentences.zh: 樞密使楊復恭遇之，以處士薦為太常博士，進度支員外郎。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Yang Fugong encountered him, recommended him as a recluse scholar for the post of Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and he advanced to external administrator in the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Yang Fugong, encountered him and recommended him as a recluse scholar for the post of Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Jun was then promoted to external administrator in the Department of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 黃巢之亂，稱疾，挾其母走商山。

translations.literal: During Huang Chao's rebellion he pleaded illness, took his mother, and fled to Shangshan.
translations.idiomatic: During Huang Chao's rebellion he pleaded illness, took his mother, and fled into the Shangshan hills.

sentences.zh: 僖宗西出，衛士食不給，漢陰令李康獻糗餌數百馱，士皆厭給。

translations.literal: When Xizong went west, the guard's rations ran short; Li Kang, magistrate of Hanyin, presented several hundred loads of dried rations, and the troops were all fully supplied.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong fled west, the imperial guard ran short of food; Li Kang, magistrate of Hanyin, presented several hundred pack-loads of dried provisions, and the troops were at last fully fed.

sentences.zh: 帝異之，曰：「爾乃及是乎？

translations.literal: The emperor was surprised and said: "You can do even this?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was astonished and said, "You can manage even this?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣安知為此，張濬教臣也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Your servant would never have known to do this — Zhang Jun taught me.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Your servant would never have known to do this — Zhang Jun taught me.

sentences.zh: 」乃急召濬至行在，再進諫議大夫。

translations.literal: " Zhang Jun was urgently summoned to the imperial camp and was promoted again to Supervisory Censor.
translations.idiomatic: " Jun was urgently summoned to the imperial camp and was promoted again to Supervisory Censor.

sentences.zh: 宰相王鐸任行營都統，奏署都統判官。

translations.literal: The chancellor Wang Duo served as overall commander of the mobile camp and memorialized to appoint Jun as judge on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor Wang Duo served as overall commander of the mobile camp and memorialized to appoint Jun as judge on his staff.

sentences.zh: 時王敬武在平盧，軍最強，累召不肯應。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Jingwu was at Pinglu; his army was the strongest; repeated summonses he refused to obey.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Jingwu held Pinglu; his army was the strongest in the land, yet repeated imperial summonses he refused to answer.

sentences.zh: 濬往說之，而敬武已臣賊，不迎使者。

translations.literal: Jun went to persuade him, but Jingwu had already submitted to the rebel and did not receive the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Jun went to persuade him, but Jingwu had already submitted to the rebels and refused to receive the envoy.

sentences.zh: 浚責之曰：「公為天子守藩，今使者賫詔至，不北面俯伏而敢侮慢，公乃未識君臣大分，何以長吏民哉？

translations.literal: Jun rebuked him: "You hold a frontier for the Son of Heaven; now an envoy arrives bearing an edict — you do not face north and prostrate yourself but dare to show insolence; you do not yet grasp the great distinction between sovereign and subject — how can you long govern officials and people?
translations.idiomatic: Jun rebuked him: "You hold a frontier post for the Son of Heaven; now an envoy arrives bearing an edict, yet you do not face north and prostrate yourself but dare to show insolence. You do not yet grasp the great distinction between sovereign and subject — how can you long govern officials and people?

sentences.zh: 」敬武愕眙愧謝。

translations.literal: " Jingwu stared in shock, ashamed, and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingwu stared in shock, ashamed, and apologized.

sentences.zh: 濬宣詔已，士按兵默默。

translations.literal: After Jun proclaimed the edict, the troops held their weapons in silence.
translations.idiomatic: After Jun proclaimed the edict, the troops stood in silence with weapons in hand.

sentences.zh: 濬召將佐至鞠場，倡言：「忠義之士當審利害。

translations.literal: Jun summoned the officers to the drill ground and declared: "Loyal and righteous men ought to weigh gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: Jun summoned the officers to the drill ground and declared, "Men of loyalty and righteousness ought to weigh gain against loss.

sentences.zh: 黃巢，販鹽虜耳。

translations.literal: Huang Chao is nothing but a salt-smuggling bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao is nothing but a salt-smuggling bandit.

sentences.zh: 舍天子而臣之，何利邪？

translations.literal: To abandon the Son of Heaven and serve him — what profit is there?
translations.idiomatic: To abandon the Son of Heaven and serve him — what profit is there in that?

sentences.zh: 今諸侯勤王者踵相接，公等據一州以觀成敗，後賊平，將安往？

translations.literal: Now feudatories rushing to aid the throne follow one after another; you hold one province and watch how things turn out — when the rebels are crushed, where will you go?
translations.idiomatic: Now feudatories rushing to aid the throne follow one after another; you hold a single province and watch how things turn out — when the rebels are crushed, where will you go?

sentences.zh: 誠能此時共誅大盜，迎天子，功名富貴可反手而取。

translations.literal: If you can now join in destroying the great bandit and welcome the emperor, fame, merit, wealth, and rank can be seized in the turning of a hand.
translations.idiomatic: If you join now in destroying the great bandit and welcoming the emperor, fame, merit, wealth, and rank can be seized in the turning of a hand.

sentences.zh: 吾憐公等舍安而陷危也。

translations.literal: I pity you for leaving safety and falling into danger.
translations.idiomatic: I pity you for leaving safety and falling into danger.

sentences.zh: 」諸將雜然曰：「諫議語是！

translations.literal: " The generals clamored: "The Supervisory Censor speaks rightly!
translations.idiomatic: " The generals clamored in reply, "The Supervisory Censor speaks rightly!

sentences.zh: 」敬武即引軍從浚西。

translations.literal: " Jingwu immediately led his army west following Jun.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingwu immediately led his army west in Jun's train.

sentences.zh: 擢濬為會軍使。

translations.literal: Jun was promoted to Commissioner for Assembling the Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was promoted to Commissioner for Assembling the Armies.

sentences.zh: 賊平，以戶部侍郎判度支。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he served as Vice Minister of Revenue with concurrent charge of the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were pacified, he served as Vice Minister of Revenue with concurrent charge of the Department of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 後再狩山南，拜同中書門下平章事，仍判度支。

translations.literal: Later when the emperor again fled south of the mountains, he was appointed co-chancellor while still overseeing revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor again fled south of the mountains, he was appointed co-chancellor while continuing to oversee revenue.

sentences.zh: 是時，朱全忠威振關東，而安居受殺李克恭，以潞州歸全忠。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Quanzhong's prestige shook the east of the Pass; An Jushou killed Li Kegong and surrendered Luzhou to Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhu Quanzhong's prestige shook the region east of the Pass; An Jushou killed Li Kegong and surrendered Luzhou to Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 全忠乃與幽州李匡威、雲州赫連鐸上言：「先帝幸梁，繇李克用與朱玫連和，請舉兵誅之，願帥兵為掎角。

translations.literal: Quanzhong then joined Li Kuangwei of Youzhou and Helian Duo of Yunzhou in a memorial: "When the late emperor went to Liang, it was because Li Keyong allied with Zhu Mei; we ask permission to raise troops to execute him and volunteer our armies as pincers.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong then joined Li Kuangwei of Youzhou and Helian Duo of Yunzhou in a memorial: "When the late emperor fled to Liang, it was because Li Keyong allied with Zhu Mei. We ask permission to raise troops and execute him, and volunteer our armies as pincers.

sentences.zh: 」帝詔文武四品以上議，皆言：「王室未寧，雖得太原，猶非所有。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered discussion among civil and military officials of the fourth rank and above; all said: "The royal house is not yet secure; even if we take Taiyuan, it would not truly be ours.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered civil and military officials of the fourth rank and above to debate the matter; all said, "The royal house is not yet secure — even if we took Taiyuan, it would not truly be ours.

sentences.zh: 」濬固爭：「先帝時，身播屯亂，蓋克用、全忠不相下也。

translations.literal: " Jun insisted: "In the late emperor's time the throne was cast into turmoil — it was because Keyong and Quanzhong would not yield to each other.
translations.idiomatic: " Jun insisted: "In the late emperor's time the throne was cast into turmoil because Keyong and Quanzhong would not yield to each other.

sentences.zh: 請因其弱討之，斷兩雄勢。

translations.literal: I ask that we strike him while he is weak and break the power of these two rivals.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we strike him while he is weak and break the power of these two rival strongmen.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「平巢，克用功第一。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "In pacifying Huang Chao, Keyong's merit was first.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "In pacifying Huang Chao, Keyong's merit ranked first.

sentences.zh: 今乘危伐之，天下其謂我何？

translations.literal: Now to attack him in his straits — what will the realm say of me?
translations.idiomatic: Now to attack him in his straits — what will the realm say of me?

sentences.zh: 」久不決。

translations.literal: " For a long time no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: " For a long time no decision was reached.

sentences.zh: 孔緯曰：「濬言萬世之利，陛下所顧一時事爾。

translations.literal: Kong Wei said: "Jun speaks of benefit for ten thousand generations; Your Majesty is concerned only with a moment's affair.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wei said, "Jun speaks of benefit for ten thousand generations, while Your Majesty is concerned only with a moment's affair.

sentences.zh: 臣見師度河，賊必破。

translations.literal: I see the army crossing the river and the enemy must be broken.
translations.idiomatic: I see the army crossing the river and the enemy surely broken.

sentences.zh: 今軍中費尚足支數年，幸聽勿疑。

translations.literal: Military expenses now suffice for several years — I pray you heed us and do not doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Military expenses now suffice for several years — I pray Your Majesty heed us and do not doubt.

sentences.zh: 」既濬、緯相倡和，帝乃決出師，詔濬為河東行營兵馬招討制置使，京兆尹孫揆為昭義節度使副之，韓建為供軍使；

translations.literal: " Once Jun and Wei voiced agreement, the emperor decided to send out the army; Jun was ordered as Commander and Commissioner for the Hedong Mobile Camp, Sun Kui the Jingzhao governor as deputy military governor of Zhaoyi, Han Jian as provision officer;
translations.idiomatic: " Once Jun and Wei spoke in unison, the emperor decided to send out the army. Jun was appointed Commander and Commissioner for the Hedong Mobile Camp; Sun Kui, governor of Jingzhao, was made deputy military governor of Zhaoyi; Han Jian was made provision officer;

sentences.zh: 以全忠、匡威、鐸並為招討使，樞密使駱全諲為行營都監，以汴甲三千為帳下；

translations.literal: Quanzhong, Kuangwei, and Duo were all made pacification commissioners; the Commissioner of Military Affairs Luo Quanyin was made overall supervisor of the camp, with three thousand Bian armies as his personal guard;
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong, Kuangwei, and Duo were all made pacification commissioners; the Commissioner of Military Affairs Luo Quanyin was made overall supervisor of the camp, with three thousand Bian troops as his personal guard;

sentences.zh: 發五十二軍，邠、寧、鄜、夏雜虜合五萬。

translations.literal: Fifty-two armies were mobilized, with mixed tribes from Bin, Ning, Fu, and Xia totaling fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty-two armies were mobilized, with mixed tribal forces from Bin, Ning, Fu, and Xia totaling fifty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 帝置酒安喜樓臨餞，濬飲酣，泣下曰：「陛下逼於賊，臣願以死除之。

translations.literal: The emperor set wine at Anxi Tower to send them off; Jun, well drunk, wept and said: "Your Majesty is pressed by rebels — your servant wishes to remove them even at the cost of death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor set out wine at Anxi Tower to send them off; Jun, well drunk, wept and said, "Your Majesty is pressed by rebels — your servant wishes to remove them even at the cost of his life.

sentences.zh: 」復恭聞不懌，率中尉等餞長樂阪，以酒屬濬，浚不肯舉。

translations.literal: " Fugong heard this with displeasure; he led the commandants of the palace armies to bid farewell at Changle Slope and offered wine to Jun, but Jun would not raise the cup.
translations.idiomatic: " Fugong heard this with displeasure; he led the commandants of the palace armies to bid farewell at Changle Slope and offered wine to Jun, but Jun would not raise the cup.

sentences.zh: 是役也濬外幸成功，而內制復恭，故銜之。

translations.literal: In this campaign Jun outwardly hoped for success but inwardly sought to check Fugong; therefore Fugong harbored a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign Jun outwardly hoped for success but inwardly sought to check Fugong; for this reason Fugong harbored a grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 先是，汴、華、邠、岐兵絕河會平陽。

translations.literal: Earlier, armies from Bian, Hua, Bin, and Qi crossed the river and assembled at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, armies from Bian, Hua, Bin, and Qi had crossed the river and assembled at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 汴將朱崇節已戍潞，濬慮汴人遂據有之，乃令揆分兵趨潞，以中人韓歸範持節護送至軍。

translations.literal: The Bian general Zhu Chongjie was already garrisoning Lu; Jun feared the Bian men would simply hold it, so he ordered Sun Kui to split forces and hurry to Lu, with the inner attendant Han Guifan bearing insignia to escort him to the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian general Zhu Chongjie was already garrisoning Lu; Jun feared the Bian troops would simply keep it for themselves, so he ordered Sun Kui to split his forces and hurry to Lu, with the inner attendant Han Guifan bearing insignia to escort him to the army.

sentences.zh: 會太原將李存孝方攻潞，揆至長子，為存孝所禽，汴人亦棄城去。

translations.literal: Just then the Taiyuan general Li Cunxiao was attacking Lu; when Sun Kui reached Changzi he was captured by Cunxiao, and the Bian men also abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Taiyuan general Li Cunxiao was attacking Lu; when Sun Kui reached Changzi he was captured by Cunxiao, and the Bian troops also abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 浚次陰地關，諸軍壁平陽。

translations.literal: Jun halted at Yindi Pass; the armies encamped at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jun halted at Yindi Pass while the armies encamped at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 存孝擊之，皆大北，委仗械去。

translations.literal: Cunxiao struck them; all suffered great defeat, abandoning weapons and armor as they fled.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao struck them; all suffered crushing defeat, abandoning weapons and armor as they fled.

sentences.zh: 濬斂眾夜遁，比明，軍失太半。

translations.literal: Jun gathered what troops he could and fled by night; by dawn more than half the army was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Jun gathered what troops he could and fled by night; by dawn more than half the army was gone.

sentences.zh: 存孝進掠晉、絳、慈、隰，其鋒甚盛。

translations.literal: Cunxiao advanced raiding Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Xi; his momentum was very fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao advanced, raiding Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Xi; his momentum was fierce.

sentences.zh: 濬間道出王屋，奔河清，桴而濟，麾下略盡。

translations.literal: Jun took a bypath through Wangwu, fled to Heqing, crossed by raft, and nearly all his followers were gone.
translations.idiomatic: Jun took a bypath through Wangwu, fled to Heqing, crossed the river by raft, and nearly all his followers were gone.

sentences.zh: 全諲飲藥死，建遁去。

translations.literal: Quan Qian drank poison and died; Jian fled.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Qian took poison and died; Han Jian escaped.

sentences.zh: 克用上書請罪，其辭悖慢，因韓歸範以聞。

translations.literal: Keyong submitted a memorial asking pardon; its wording was insolent and disrespectful, and it was reported through Han Guifan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong memorialized asking forgiveness in language so insolent that Han Guifan carried it to the court.

sentences.zh: 朝廷震動，即日下詔罷濬為武昌軍節度使，三貶繡州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: The court was shaken; that same day an edict removed Jun from office as military commissioner of Wuchang and demoted him three ranks to army registrar of Xiuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court reeled; the same day an edict stripped Jun of the Wuchang commission and demoted him three ranks to army registrar of Xiuzhou.

sentences.zh: 全忠為申請，詔聽使便。

translations.literal: Quanzhong petitioned on his behalf, and an edict permitted him to travel as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong interceded for him, and the throne allowed him to travel as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 濬乃至藍田依韓建。

translations.literal: Jun then reached Lantian and relied on Han Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Jun made his way to Lantian and took refuge with Han Jian.

sentences.zh: 及韋昭度死，復用緯為宰相，故濬亦拜兵部尚書，領天下租庸使。

translations.literal: When Wei Zhaodu died, Wei was again used as chief minister, and therefore Jun was also appointed Minister of War and charged as commissioner for realm-wide rent and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei Zhaodu died, Kong Wei returned to the premiership, and Jun was named Minister of War and put in charge of empire-wide rent and corvée.

sentences.zh: 將復用，克用上言：「若朝以濬為相，暮請以兵見。

translations.literal: When he was about to be used again, Keyong memorialized: "If the court makes Jun chief minister, by evening I ask to meet you with arms.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to be recalled, Li Keyong wrote, "If the court names Jun chief minister, by evening I shall come with an army."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " The appointment was halted.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，罷使，拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the Qianning era he was removed from the commission and appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianning he was relieved of the commission and named Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 上疏乞骸骨，遷左僕射致仕，居洛長水墅。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to surrender his bones, was transferred to Left Vice Director with retirement, and dwelt at his Changshui villa in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to retire, was made Left Vice Director emeritus, and lived at his Changshui villa in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 雖自屏處，然朝廷得失，時時言之。

translations.literal: Though he secluded himself, he still spoke from time to time of the court's gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Though he kept apart from office, he still spoke out now and then on what the court did right or wrong.

sentences.zh: 劉季述亂，濬徒步入洛，泣諭張全義，並致書諸藩，請謀王室之難。

translations.literal: When Liu Jishu rebelled, Jun walked alone into Luoyang, weeping as he urged Zhang Quanyi, and also sent letters to the various circuits asking them to plot against the royal house's peril.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jishu rebelled, Jun walked alone into Luoyang in tears to plead with Zhang Quanyi and wrote to the provinces urging them to rescue the throne.

sentences.zh: 王師範起兵青州，欲取濬為謀主，不克。

translations.literal: Wang Shifan raised troops in Qingzhou and wished to take Jun as strategist, but could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shifan raised an army in Qingzhou hoping to make Jun his strategist, but failed.

sentences.zh: 全忠脅帝東遷，濬聞曰：「乘輿卜洛，則大事去矣。

translations.literal: Quanzhong coerced the emperor to move east; Jun heard and said: "If the imperial carriage is divined for Luoyang, the great affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong forced the emperor east, Jun said, "If the imperial carriage is sent to Luoyang, the dynasty is finished."

sentences.zh: 」蓋知其將篡也。

translations.literal: " For he understood that Quanzhong was about to usurp.
translations.idiomatic: He had seen that usurpation was coming.

sentences.zh: 全忠畏濬構它鎮兵，使全義遣牙將如盜者夜圍墅殺之，屠其家百餘人，實天復二年十二月。

translations.literal: Quanzhong feared Jun would stir other circuits' troops; he had Quanyi send military aides like bandits to surround the villa by night and kill him, slaughtering more than a hundred of his household—this was in the twelfth month of the second year of Tianfu.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Jun would rally other provinces, Quanzhong had Quanyi send men like robbers to surround the villa by night and kill him, slaughtering more than a hundred of his kin—in the twelfth month of Tianfu year two.

sentences.zh: 始，濬素厚永寧史葉彥，彥知其謀，以告濬子格。

translations.literal: At first Jun had long been close to Ye Yan, military commissioner of Yongning; Yan knew the plot and told Jun's son Ge.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had long been close to Ye Yan of Yongning; Yan learned of the plot and warned Jun's son Ge.

sentences.zh: 濬度不免，父子相持泣曰：「留則俱死，不如去以存吾嗣。

translations.literal: Jun judged he could not escape; father and son clung weeping and said: "If we stay we die together—better to go and preserve our line.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no escape, father and son wept in each other's arms: "If we stay we die together—go, and save our line."

sentences.zh: 」格拜而辭，彥率士三十人送之，溯漢入蜀，後事王建。

translations.literal: " Ge bowed and took leave; Yan led thirty men to escort him, went up the Han into Shu, and later served Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Ge bowed farewell; Yan led thirty men to escort him up the Han into Shu, where he later served Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 少子播，間道走淮南，依楊行密。

translations.literal: The younger son Bo fled by hidden paths to Huainan and relied on Yang Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: The younger son Bo stole away to Huainan and attached himself to Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 時行密得承制除拜，播請每除吏，必紫極宮玄宗像前致制誥於案，乃出之，示不忘朝廷，且欲雪家冤而不克。

translations.literal: At the time Xingmi received provisional authority for appointments and dismissals; Bo requested that whenever an official was appointed, the edict of appointment must be set before the image of Emperor Xuanzong in the Ziji Palace, and only then issued—showing he had not forgotten the court, and wishing also to avenge his family's wrong but unable.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi then held provisional appointment powers; Bo insisted that every commission be laid before Emperor Xuanzong's image in the Ziji Palace before issue—a sign he had not forgotten the throne and a vain hope of avenging his family.

sentences.zh: 終廣陵。

translations.literal: He ended his days at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：唐之季，嗣君暗庸，天穢其德久矣。

translations.literal: The encomium says: In Tang's late age the succeeding rulers were dim and mediocre; Heaven had long reviled their virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: In Tang's decline the heirs were dull and inept; Heaven had long withheld favor from their house.

sentences.zh: 纖人柄朝，靡謀不乖。

translations.literal: Petty men held the court; no counsel failed to go awry.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men held the court, and counsel went wrong at every turn.

sentences.zh: 如畋、鐸皆社稷之才，當大過之世，為天下倡。

translations.literal: Men such as Tian and Duo were talents of the altars of state; in an age of great excess they became leaders for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Tian and Duo were pillars of the state; in an age of excess they stood as examples for the realm.

sentences.zh: 扶支王室，幾致中興。

translations.literal: They propped the royal house and nearly brought about restoration.
translations.idiomatic: They braced the throne and nearly restored the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 俄而為逆豎亂宦所乘，功業無所成就。

translations.literal: Before long they were overtaken by rebellious ruffians and disorderly eunuchs, and their achievements came to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they were undone by rebel chiefs and meddling eunuchs, and their work came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 浚以亂止亂，悖繆厥心，悲夫！

translations.literal: Jun sought to end disorder with disorder; perverse and wrong was his heart—lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Jun would end chaos with chaos; his heart was perverse—how lamentable!
